long_biography.plain_text:
At a moment when Ukraine's agricultural markets were being remade, Yuriy Kosiuk moved from commodity brokerage and furniture trading into grain, then founded MHP in 1998. The company bought a feed mill and poultry farm, launched the Nasha Ryaba chicken brand and linked crop production, feed, breeding, processing and distribution in one platform. Its 2008 London flotation made MHP the first Ukrainian agricultural company to raise foreign equity through an IPO.

Kosiuk remains MHP's chief executive and controls 59.7% through WTI Trading. Under his leadership, the business expanded from a national poultry producer into an international food company with operations in Ukraine, Spain and southeastern Europe. Trained as a meat-processing engineer, he briefly left the chief executive role for several months to serve in Ukraine's presidential administration before returning. The state named him a Hero of Ukraine for contributions to agriculture and agricultural technology.
